newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar is too high, new govt solution - Cullen.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar is too high, new govt solution - Cullen.

text.p: Opposition Labour Party finance spokesman Michael Cullen on Thursday said the New Zealand dollar was too high.

"It is too high. But making ACC competitive is not going to lower the dollar. In fact if those sort of moves were (made) we would actually increase the dollar further," Cullen told Reuters as he went into formal talks with nationalist NZ First over the shape of the next government.
Reform of the Accident Rehabilitation and Compensation Corporation (ACC) has been identified by employer and export groups as one area of concern.
Asked whether a change of government was needed to lower the dollar, Cullen said: "Absolutely".

Cullen, who Labour leader Helen Clark has identified as the sole candidate for the finance portfolio if she leads the next government, said the length of coalition talks was having an impact on investment.
"People will be holding off making investment decisions. If it is only a short period of time it doesn't too matter but if it goes on for very long it does start to have an influence," Cullen said.
On Thursday a group of Wellington civic and business leaders said the prolonged coalition negotiations were inhibiting investment and urged the parties to speed up a resolution.
Clark said Wellington mayors would have to patient.
"I think everybody underestimated the amount of time it was going to take and I include myself.

"I think there is no question everything is in hiatus. I suspect people aren't spending as much as they normally would, not investing as much as they normally would and not employing as much, and of course that's a concern. But we are working as fast as we can," Clark said.

Thursday's talks were the seventh between NZ First and Labour. NZ First is also negotiating with the conservative National Party over the shape of the next government. It holds the balance of power after an election on October 12.
